Candidate command installation -> recipient guards and retained state -> AcceptReply construction -> ballot comparison -> local commitment threshold
Execution recovery request -> recover reuses existing bookkeeping -> makeBallot and Prepare broadcast -> reply processing
counterevidence: The run loop serially dispatches protocol handlers. The proposed repeated broadcasts arise from successive handler invocations and need no concurrent protocol-handler execution.

SendMsg holds the shared replica mutex while emitting the tag, marshaling the payload, and flushing. Successful sends therefore have a serialization protection; it does not establish unique participant counting.

ConnectToPeers creates a listener for each remote peer. replicaListener knows rid but forwards only the decoded object to the protocol channel. No contributor filtering is visible in this listener or the Paxos dispatch loop.

The constructor initializes PreferredPeerOrder as a permutation. ComputeClosestPeers either constructs an order using latency and participant-ID tie breaking or sorts the existing entries. Repeated broadcasts do not require duplicate peer-order entries. Exact recipient coverage under latency-table sorting remains unestablished.

handleAccept installs commands for missing or eligible noncommitted records, rejects lower ballots, and preserves committed records. Equal-ballot replies retaining different commands still require a justified history.

handleAcceptReply ignores lower ballots, treats higher ballots as nacks, and returns for committed instances. The proposed discriminator concerns two equal-ballot replies consumed before the first commitment.
handlePropose initializes fresh counters. recover initializes them when bookkeeping is absent, but reuses existing bookkeeping otherwise.

A three-participant configuration with F=1 requires only one remote contribution. The proposed insufficient-support schedule instead uses the constructor-supported five-participant configuration with F=2; no actual deployment size has been established.

The selected constructor enables execution and the shared constructor sets Dreply=true and Durable=false. The immediate check must stop at commitment and cannot infer a pre-execution client reply or durable acceptance.

README identifies the selected implementation as classic Paxos, providing protocol-intent context. It does not explicitly specify distinct-reply accounting or independently establish the proposed local acceptance-support contract.
unknowns: Whether the actual Prepare, PrepareReply, Accept, and AcceptReply codecs preserve the fields and stream boundaries required by the proposed repeated-request history.
Whether RPC registration and lookup deliver each relevant decoded message to its intended channel.
Whether a supported latency-table configuration, including nil handling, permits the proposed channel-delivery schedule without an earlier failure.
Whether a legally reachable committed recipient can report the attempted ballot while retaining commands different from the current candidate.
Whether one instance and ballot always identifies one command batch across prepare completion, retry, recovery, and intervening handlers.
How attempt validity is maintained when existing counters survive recovery or ballot changes; the visible paths do not reset them.
What establishes the candidate-command association of the implicit local contribution across all relevant paths; prepare completion installs commands and ACCEPTED status but does not assign vbal.
The actual deployment's configured and master-returned membership sizes are not supplied. The five-participant scenario is a proposed supported configuration, not an observed deployment.
Recipient coverage under the latency-table sorting branch and whether independent recovery interferes before the stopping observation.

The precise applicable local acceptance-support obligation and its independent oracle remain to be finalized. The proposed oracle counts distinct replicas with actual candidate-command installation events, independently of acceptOKs.
history.trigger_rationale: The acquired shared-runtime source resolves two decisive gaps in the same discriminator. WriteQuorumSize is F+1, ReadQuorumSize is N-F, and runReplica derives F from configured replica addresses; a consistent five-participant setup therefore needs two remote acceptance contributions. Separately, replicaListener schedules a channel delivery for each successfully decoded protocol message without visibly retaining rid in that delivery or filtering repeated contributors. Combined with handlePrepareReply broadcasting Accept on every equal-ballot reply at or above its threshold, this supports a prospective application-generated repeated-response schedule. Codec, registry, and latency-helper behavior remain concrete causal dependencies before treating that schedule as executable.
